subtitle: Enter your product details. Get a ready-to-publish description for Amazon, Shopify, Etsy, or social.
resultDisclaimer: Review before publishing. Verify all product claims and specifications against actual product details.
whatIsText: Writing product descriptions is tedious. Every product needs one, every platform has its own format, and the copy directly affects conversion. This tool takes your product details and generates a description tailored to the platform you're selling on — Amazon, Shopify, Etsy, or social — in the style and length you choose.
tip1: List specific features, not benefits. The model will turn features into benefits. If you write "benefits" you'll get vague output. Write "GOTS-certified organic cotton, snap closure, 0-24 months" and let the model sell it.
tip2: Include the audience. A baby onesie for eco-conscious parents reads differently than one for budget shoppers. Tell the model who it's for.
tip3: Match the style to the brand. Luxury brands should use the Luxury style. Mass-market products use Professional or Friendly. Kids' products can use Playful.
tip4: Choose the right platform. Amazon and Shopify have very different formatting expectations. If you sell on both, generate two versions.
faq1a: Yes. It runs on Cloudflare Workers AI with a free daily quota. Normal use won't hit limits.
faq2q: Will the description rank on Amazon?
faq2a: The Amazon format front-loads keywords naturally, which is a starting point for search visibility. But real Amazon ranking depends on your backend keywords, category, reviews, and sales velocity. The description is one input among many.
faq3a: No. The prompt explicitly tells the model not to invent features, materials, or specifications not in your input. However, always review the output — AI can occasionally rephrase things in ways that overstate what you provide.
faq4q: Can I use it for non-physical products?
faq4a: Yes. It works for digital products, courses, software, and services. Just describe the "product" in the features field — what it does, what's included, and who it's for.
faq5a: You should. The output is a polished draft, not a finished description. Add brand-specific details, adjust the tone to match your site, and verify any factual claims before publishing.
disclaimer: Note: This tool generates draft descriptions. Always review, verify claims, and edit before publishing.
footer: Runs on Cloudflare Workers AI. Your text is not stored.

f1d: Amazon bullets, Shopify storytelling, Etsy charm, or a social hook — matched to where you sell.
f2d: List raw specs and let the model turn them into copy that sells.
f3d: Professional, friendly, luxury or playful — and it never adds specs you didn't list.
ph2: Example: 100% GOTS-certified organic cotton. Hypoallergenic and safe for sensitive skin. Snap closure for easy changing. Available in sizes 0-24 months. Machine washable.
ph3: New parents who care about sustainability
howIntro: Features in, marketplace-ready copy out. Three fields.
how1d: A plain descriptive name works better than a model number. The name is what the copy anchors on.
how2d: Bullet points are fine: material, size, capacity, what it replaces. Do not worry about wording yet.
how3d: Amazon wants scannable bullets, Shopify allows a longer story, Etsy rewards a warmer first person voice.
whenTitle: When to use it, when not to
use1d: You have specs from the supplier and no copy. This turns the spec sheet into a first draft.
use2d: The same product needs different formatting on Amazon and Etsy; rewrite instead of copying.
use3d: Generate a benefit-led version and a spec-led version, then let the conversion numbers decide.
use4d: Consistent structure across fifty listings matters more than perfect prose on one.

faq6a: It aims for the length you choose, but check the final count against each marketplace: Amazon bullets cap at 500 characters, titles at 200.
faq7q: Can it make claims like "best" or "cures"?
faq7a: It avoids unverifiable medical and superlative claims. Add only claims you can substantiate with a certificate or test.
faq8q: Is the copy unique per product?
faq8a: Each request is written from the features you provide. Two products with identical features will produce similar copy, so add the differences.
